title: The battle over bike lanes needs a mindset shift ｜ 自行车道之争需要转变观念

sents.en: Five years ago, the city of Queens, New York, announced that it would be putting bike lanes onto a stretch of Skillman Ave · and removing 116 parking spots.
sents.cn: 五年前，纽约皇后区宣布将在斯基尔曼大道（SkillmanAve）的一段铺设自行车道，并取消116个停车位。

sents.en: Cyclists loved the plan, but local business owners got very angry.
sents.cn: 骑行者喜欢这个计划，但当地商家非常愤怒。

sents.en: Taking out those parking spots, as they argued at protests and in letters to the city council, would ruin stores and restaurants along Skillman.
sents.cn: 他们在抗议活动和写给市议会的信中辩称，取消这些停车位会毁掉斯基尔曼沿线的商店和餐馆。

sents.en: ·Parking here is already a nightmare,· one shouted at a protest rally.
sents.cn: "这里的停车已经是一场噩梦了，"有人在抗议集会上喊道。

sents.en: But the bike lanes were a done deal, and soon they were in place.
sents.cn: 但自行车道已成定局，很快便铺设完成。

sents.en: Early this year, Jesse Coburn · an investigative writer with Streetsblog New York · wondered whether those predictions of economic collapse came true.
sents.cn: 今年早些时候，《纽约街博客》（StreetsblogNewYork）的调查记者杰西∙科本（JesseCoburn）想知道那些经济崩溃的预言是否成真。

sents.en: So he asked the city's Department of Finance to give him a few years' worth of sales figures for that stretch of Skillman Ave.
sents.cn: 于是他向市财政局索要了那段斯基尔曼大道几年的销售数据。

sents.en: How had the businesses on that street fared?
sents.cn: 那条街上的生意经营得如何？

sents.en: Quite well, it turns out.
sents.cn: 结果显示相当不错。

sents.en: In the year after the bike lanes arrived, businesses on Skillman saw sales rise by 12 percent, compared to 3 percent for Queens in general.
sents.cn: 自行车道建好后的那一年，斯基尔曼沿线商家的销售额增长了12%，而整个皇后区的增幅仅为3%。

sents.en: What's more, that section of road saw new businesses open, while Queens overall had a net loss.
sents.cn: 此外，那段道路上有新店开业，而皇后区整体却出现了净减少。

sents.en: The thing is, the actual merchants along Skillman?
sents.cn: 问题是，斯基尔曼沿线的真正商家们？

sents.en: They didn't believe it.
sents.cn: 他们并不相信。

sents.en: When Coburn spoke to them and described what he'd found, only a few store owners admitted the lanes had helped.
sents.cn: 当科本和他们交谈并说明自己的发现时，只有少数店主承认自行车道带来了帮助。

sents.en: Many still insisted the lanes were killing their part of the city.
sents.cn: 许多人仍坚称，这些车道正在毁掉他们所在的城区。

sents.en: And emotions ran hot: Someone scattered tacks (大头钉) on the bike lane.
sents.cn: 情绪一度十分激烈：有人把大头钉撒在了自行车道上。

sents.en: This little story turns out to be a fascinating glimpse at the challenges cities face as they try to update their urban infrastructure · to clean up the air, reduce greenhouse emissions, and speed up travel by making towns more bike-friendly.
sents.cn: 这个小故事恰好让人窥见城市在更新基础设施——净化空气、减少温室气体排放，并通过让城镇更适宜骑行来加快出行——时所面临的挑战。

sents.en: There's a rising amount of data showing that installing bike lanes and making streets more pedestrian-friendly boosts the economic fortunes of a place.
sents.cn: 越来越多的数据表明，铺设自行车道、让街道更利于行人，能提升一个地方的经济发展。

sents.en: Removing cars and parking spots works.
sents.cn: 取消汽车和停车位确实有效。

sents.en: But the folks who run local businesses simply aren't convinced, even when their own street performs.
sents.cn: 但经营本地生意的人就是不为所动，即便他们自己那条街表现良好。

sents.en: Given that sort of mess, can political fights over bike lanes ever end?
sents.cn: 面对这种混乱局面，关于自行车道的政治之争难道会有终止的一天吗？

sents.en: In 2013, researchers at New York City's Department of Transportation studied seven stretches of road that had installed bike lanes or created pedestrian-friendly areas.
sents.cn: 2013年，纽约市交通局的研究人员研究了七段铺设了自行车道或建成步行友好区域的道路。

sents.en: The city analyzed the data for businesses along those routes and found that by the third year sales grew faster on five of the streets than in the district overall, on average · up to five times faster, in fact.
sents.cn: 该市分析了沿这些路线的商家数据，发现到第三年，其中五条街道的销售额增速高于全区平均水平——事实上最快可达全区平均水平的五倍。

sents.en: Beyond New York, a survey of research from 23 cities found that bike lanes and pedestrian-friendly design didn't hurt local retail and food stores.
sents.cn: 在纽约之外，一项涵盖23座城市的研究综述发现，自行车道和步行友好设计并未损害当地零售和食品商店。

sents.en: (·Fears of disastrous consequences for local businesses are unfounded,· the researchers concluded.) More recent work has shown roughly the same.
sents.cn: （"对本地商家会遭受灾难性后果的担忧是没有根据的，"研究人员总结道。）更近期的研究也得出了大体相同的结论。

sents.en: The truth is that in fairly dense areas, bikes are more efficient at moving people around.
sents.cn: 事实是，在相当密集的区域，自行车在运送人群方面更高效。

sents.en: You might lose one car driver's business · but you gain shoppers who now can arrive more easily on bikes.
sents.cn: 你或许会失去一位开车顾客的生意——但你也会赢得现在能更便捷地骑车而来的购物者。

sents.en: ·Cyclists and pedestrians are consumers too,· notes Professor Susan Handy.
sents.cn: "骑行者和行人也是消费者，"苏珊∙汉迪（SusanHandy）教授指出。

sents.en: Plus, streets redesigned for bikes and pedestrians tend to become more pleasant places to hang around, so ·in a lot of cases, that's created much nicer environments that are really good for those businesses.·
sents.cn: 此外，为自行车和行人重新设计的街道往往变得更宜人、更适合逗留，因此"在很多情况下，这创造了更美好的环境，对这些商家确实大有裨益。"

sents.en: Mom-and-pop shops are usually pretty quick at recognizing situations that will help their bottom lines.
sents.cn: 夫妻店通常能很快察觉到有利于其利润的情况。

sents.en: So why the blind spot here?
sents.cn: 那么为何在这里却视而不见？

sents.en: Perhaps it's that attention focuses on horror stories · and some merchants do get hit when bike lanes come in.
sents.cn: 也许是因为人们的注意力都集中在那些可怕的故事上——而且确实有部分商家在自行车道建起时受到了冲击。

sents.en: I spoke to Cindy Hughes, a hairdresser (理发师) in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
sents.cn: 我采访了马萨诸塞州剑桥市的理发师辛迪∙休斯（CindyHughes）。

sents.en: She said business fell by at least 40 percent when the city removed nearby parking to put in a bike lane.
sents.cn: 她说，当市政部门取消附近停车位、改建自行车道后，她的生意至少下滑了40%。

sents.en: The majority of her customers drive, with many coming from nearby towns.
sents.cn: 她的大多数顾客都开车，其中许多人来自周边城镇。

sents.en: Only a very few have shifted to cycling, and even those almost certainly won't cycle in Boston's snowy winters.
sents.cn: 只有极少数人改骑自行车，而即便这些人，在波士顿多雪的冬天也几乎肯定不会骑车。

sents.en: So while Hughes supports bike lanes · ·cyclists deserve to be safe· · she sees the parking loss as an existential risk.
sents.cn: 因此，尽管休斯支持自行车道——"骑行者理应安全"——她仍将失去停车位视为生存威胁。

sents.en: ·Look, 90 percent of my customers drive,· she told me.
sents.cn: "听着，我90%的顾客都开车，"她告诉我。

sents.en: ·For our business, the bike lanes are way worse than Covid was.·
sents.cn: "对我们的生意来说，自行车道比新冠疫情还要糟糕。"

sents.en: For others, the pushback is cultural, says Henry Grabar, a writer for the Slate Magazine.
sents.cn: 《Slate》杂志的撰稿人亨利∙格拉巴尔（HenryGrabar）说，对另一些人而言，抵制是出于文化因素。

sents.en: Small business owners are frequently drivers who commute from other parts of the city by car, Grabar points out.
sents.cn: 格拉巴尔指出，小商贩往往是从城市其他地方开车通勤的驾驶者。

sents.en: They're also often longtime locals.
sents.cn: 他们也常常是扎根此地已久的老住户。

sents.en: ·They tend to be people with deep roots in the city, who have hung around since before the neighborhood became what it is today,· he adds.
sents.cn: "他们往往是与这座城市渊源深厚的人，在周边社区变成今天这般模样之前就一直待在这里，"他补充道。

sents.en: Driving around town in a car is so normal to them that cycling seems weird and unusual · despite its boost from Covid, when bike sales exploded by 75 percent.
sents.cn: 对他们来说，开车在城里转悠再正常不过，以至于骑行显得古怪而不寻常——尽管骑行在新冠疫情期间因自行车销量猛增75%而有所兴起。

sents.en: Psychology beats all!
sents.cn: 心理因素压倒一切！

sents.en: Who knew, right?
sents.cn: 谁会想到，对吧？

sents.en: The fierce divide between store owners and bike-lane advocates seems similar to our larger culture wars over climate change.
sents.cn: 店主与自行车道支持者之间的激烈对立，似乎类似于我们在气候变化问题上更宏大的文化之争。

sents.en: If we've learned anything about culture wars, it's that data isn't much good at changing minds.
sents.cn: 如果说我们从文化之争中学到了什么，那就是：数据并不怎么擅长改变人的想法。

sents.en: When Janette Sadik-Khan was the head of New York City's Transportation Department back in the early 2000s, she oversaw a rollout (推出) of bike lanes — and got angry blowback from residents and business owners who claimed there weren't enough cyclists to justify installing lanes.
sents.cn: 本世纪初，当贾妮特∙萨迪克-汗（JanetteSadik-Khan）担任纽约市交通局局长时，她监督推行了自行车道，却遭到居民和商家的愤怒反弹，他们声称没有足够多的骑行者来证明建车道合理。

sents.en: Now, she notes ironically, the lanes are so full of activity that opponents have turned to claiming the problem is the opposite: There are too many cyclists getting in the way of cars.
sents.cn: 如今，她颇具讽刺意味地指出，这些车道如此繁忙，以至于反对者转而声称问题恰恰相反：骑行者太多，挡了汽车的道

sents.en: Maybe bike lanes will always be charged with emotion, until enough of the public is finally concerned about climate change — and it seems reckless (鲁莽的) to not have them.
sents.cn: 也许自行车道将永远充满情绪色彩，直到足够多的公众最终真正关心气候变化——而到那时，没有自行车道似乎倒显得鲁莽了。

sents.en: O) Crises, after all, have a way of opening people's eyes to possibilities.
sents.cn: O）毕竟，危机总有一种让人看到可能性的方式。

sents.en: During Covid, restaurants and cafes lost so much business that cities nationwide began allowing them to build curbside seating areas where people could sit, safely, in the open air.
sents.cn: 新冠期间，餐厅和咖啡馆生意损失惨重，全国各地的城市开始允许它们在路边搭建座位区，让人们在户外安全就坐。

sents.en: It greatly reduced parking · but because, well, shop owners didn't see any way around it.
sents.cn: 这大幅减少了停车位——但话说回来，商家也别无他法。

sents.en: Customers loved the outdoor seating so much that cities are making it permanent: A New York City study of several streets closed during Covid found storeowners making more than before, and diners enjoying the outdoor lifestyle.
sents.cn: 顾客如此热爱户外座位，以至于城市正将其变为永久设施：纽约市一项针对新冠期间封闭的数条街道的研究发现，店主比以往赚得更多，食客也享受着户外生活方式。

sents.en: If data won't change minds, customers might.
sents.cn: 如果数据改变不了人心，顾客或许可以。
